lines.text: Yrsa. I can keep you all warm. But only if I claim you.
If you accept, you're mine. Your warmth. Your food. Your safety. For good. I don't know how to give that back.
Southern boy, I am seventy winters old. Nobody has offered to be responsible for me in fifty years. I accept.
A thread of cold ran out of my chest and into her. And the frost on her furs began to melt.
Then the children, one by one. I didn't know their names yet. I meant it anyway.
Rune said yes before I'd finished asking. The smallest girl couldn't speak. She just held my finger. That was enough.
No light. No rings. No miracle. Just warmth, coming back into twelve people, one at a time.
Outside, Wren told me later, they were losing. The wyrm was tearing at the rubble, digging its way toward me.
It wants warm? Then we give it warm!
Kell had carried a stove down for the children. Garrow lit it, and ran with it up the tunnels, shouting. And the wyrm followed the warmth.
Out into the daylight. Straight at Tobin's Mistake.
Now, lads! Fire!
The first harpoon went through its jaw. The second through its side. The chains snapped tight.
Ash seized one chain in his teeth. The white wolf seized the other. Together they dragged its head down into the snow.
Wren drew her father's bow, and put an arrow through its eye.
One eye for one eye.
And Oswin drove the last harpoon down behind its skull, with both hands and every ring he had.
The wyrm shuddered once, and was still.
Somebody tell Tobin it wasn't a mistake.
In the dark, I felt the fight end. Wren's thread, Oswin's, Ash's, all stopped hurting at once.
And I felt twelve new threads, every one of them pulling cold into me, steady as falling snow.
By the time they dug us out, my fingertips were black.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter thirty-nine, coming soon.
